raw.title: Principal Software Engineer
raw.excerpt: POS-5690About the TeamThe Observability team owns the internal platform that gives every HubSpot engineer real visibility into how their systems behave in production.
raw.description:
POS-5690

About the Team

The Observability team owns the internal platform that gives every HubSpot engineer real visibility into how their systems behave in production. We build and operate the distributed tracing, metrics, alerting, and logging infrastructure that spans hundreds of microservices, billions of daily events, and thousands of engineers who depend on that signal to ship reliably.

We are now investing in the next generation of this platform. As HubSpot deploys AI agents and ML-powered features across the product, the team is building the tracing and telemetry primitives that make it possible to understand, debug, and trust what those systems are doing in production. This is greenfield, technically interesting work at a scale few companies operate at and we are looking for a Principal Engineer to help lead it.

About the Role

We are seeking a Principal Software Engineer to be the technical anchor for HubSpot’s Observability platform. This role sits at the intersection of large-scale distributed systems, developer platform design, and AI observability. A big part of this role is working horizontally across a large engineering org and setting patterns and standards that make it easier for teams to instrument, alert on, and reason about their services. You will also shape how we trace and understand our growing fleet of AI agents and ML systems in production: a technically distinct and increasingly critical problem.

Key Expectations

  • Observability Platform Architecture: Define the patterns and evolution of HubSpot’s core telemetry platform — distributed tracing, metrics, and structured logging — at a scale that spans hundreds of services and billions of daily events. Set the standards for how instrumentation is done across a large, polyglot engineering organization.
  • AI & Agentic Observability: Lead the technical strategy for tracing and understanding AI agents and ML-powered systems in production. Define the primitives, telemetry standards, and debugging workflows that help product engineers understand what their models and agents are doing — and build trust in those systems over time. This is greenfield and consequential work.
  • High-Cardinality, High-Throughput Systems: Architect telemetry pipelines and storage systems that handle high-cardinality data at high throughput without blowing up cost or query latency. Make principled tradeoffs between sampling, fidelity, retention, and developer ergonomics.
  • Hands-on, High-Leverage Builder: Ship production code. Lead design reviews and take high-impact initiatives end-to-end, from prototype to production system at scale. Stay close to the systems you build and be the person who can debug the hardest problems when they surface.
  • Developer Experience & Adoption: Design the instrumentation APIs and libraries that product engineers reach for, making correct observability the path of least resistance. Drive OpenTelemetry adoption across a large, polyglot codebase. Build the tooling that turns raw telemetry into actionable signal for teams operating at speed.
  • Production Intelligence & Reliability Patterns: Define patterns for SLO/SLI design, alerting philosophy, and how teams graduate from reactive to proactive incident response. Push for simplicity in a domain that wants to get complicated, and consistency where tooling can drift across a large organization.
  • Technical Leadership & Influence: Partner with infrastructure, platform, and product engineering teams to understand their signal gaps and close them. Influence technical strategy alongside engineering leadership, translating observability constraints and opportunities into product and operational decisions. Mentor senior engineers and tech leads, driving thoughtful design decisions and capturing learnings from major incidents and large-scale migrations.

What You Bring

  • Platform-Builder Experience: Proven experience building observability or telemetry tooling for internal engineering teams, rather than simply consuming it. You understand how to architect developer platforms that serve thousands of engineers across a large organization, backed by deep operational instincts and hard-earned expertise.
  • Telemetry Systems Depth: Deep expertise navigating trade-offs in telemetry pipeline design across high-cardinality data, dynamic sampling, query latency, retention economics, and data fidelity. Strong technical fluency with OpenTelemetry, distributed tracing engines, metric backends, and large-scale log ingestion infrastructure.
  • Incident Automation & Operational Excellence: Proven track record linking telemetry signals directly to automated operational workflows. You have designed architecture for real-time telemetry triggers that power automated remediation, dynamic runbooks, or AI-assisted root-cause diagnosis across microservices environments.

Why This Role, Why Now

HubSpot is scaling fast — more engineers, more microservices, more AI systems running in production — and the Observability platform is at an inflection point. The foundations are solid, but the next phase requires a different kind of investment: rethinking cardinality economics, making OpenTelemetry the default across a large polyglot org, and building an entirely new layer of AI tracing that doesn’t yet exist.

This Principal Engineer will have a direct line of sight from the architecture they design to the engineering outcomes we measure: incident response times, adoption rates, developer satisfaction, and the trust that product teams place in their production signal. The AI observability layer in particular is greenfield — there is no playbook to follow, which is exactly what makes this the right moment for the right person.

If you want to build the platform that helps thousands of engineers understand what their systems are doing — including systems powered by AI that are genuinely hard to see inside — this is the role.

Pay & Benefits

The cash compensation below includes base salary, on-target commission for employees in eligible roles, and annual bonus targets under HubSpot’s bonus plan for eligible roles. In addition to cash compensation, some roles are eligible to participate in HubSpot’s equity plan to receive restricted stock units (RSUs). Some roles may also be eligible for overtime pay. Individual compensation packages are tailored to your skills, experience, qualifications, and other job-related reasons.

Description

🤓 TripleTen is an EdTech company that designs and runs tech career learning programs for the US and Latin American markets. We've been doing it for over five years, teaching complete beginners — people with no prior tech background — through cohort-based programs built on our own platform and curriculum, developed in partnership with Nebius AI. Our team is fully remote and globally distributed, and we serve a large, active student base across both regions.

As our Senior User Acquisition Manager, you'll own one of our largest paid channels end to end — strategy, budget allocation, creative direction and funnel performance. This is a high-ticket product with a long, partly offline sales cycle: the sale doesn't happen in the ad account, it happens weeks later on a call with our sales team. Your job is to understand that whole path and move it.

This is a hands-on, single-owner role: no layer of buyers between you and the account. Reporting to our Marketing Lead, you'll work directly with creative, sales and analytics.

What you will do

  • Own the channel, not the tasks: Strategy, campaign structure, budget allocation and results are yours. You keep the account impeccable — nothing runs that shouldn't — and you defend your numbers to the business.
  • Run a continuous flow of tests across audiences, funnels and creatives. Each launch starts with a written plan — hypothesis, metric, budget, decision rule.
  • Read the whole funnel: CPL and lead volume are the beginning of the story, not the end. You track lead → SQL → sale.

Requirements

  • UA Expertise: 3+ years in User Acquisition, including personal ownership of Meta accounts at $50k+/month. Ownership means you set the strategy.
  • Relevant Recent Experience: In the last 2–3 years, products with a considered purchase and a long or offline conversion — education, B2B, fintech, real estate, healthcare or similar.
  • Analytical Rigor: Comfortable well past the ad account — lead quality, CAC, ROI, and reporting you build for yourself. You can name a change of yours that moved a down-funnel metric, and explain how you knew it worked.
  • Structured Thinking on Paper: Launch plans, test maps and post-mortems are a habit.
  • A Position You Can Defend: You've seen a problem nobody assigned to you, dug into the data, proposed a solution and carried it through. You argue with your manager when you think they're wrong — with evidence.
  • Creative Intuition: While you don't need to be a designer, you must have a deep understanding of visual hooks, messaging, and what drives engagement in the current Meta landscape.
  • Adaptability: A fast-paced, remote-first environment where you work independently and own your results.
  • Language Proficiency: Working proficiency in English (B2+ preferred).

What we can offer you

  • Competitive compensation.
  • Full-time remote contract with a flexible schedule.
  • A close-knit, international team of thoughtful and driven professionals.
  • All software licenses and remote work tools you need to be successful in a remote working environment (Slack, Miro, Notion, Zoom, etc).

raw.description:
About Qevlar AI

Qevlar is a B2B SaaS scale-up on a mission to boost the productivity of cybersecurity teams with Artificial Intelligence. We build an AI platform that transitions Security Operations Centers from reactive to proactive units through autonomous security alert investigations.

In just three years, we have:

  • Raised a total of $44m in series-A & seed rounds from EQT Ventures, Forgepoint Capital and Partech

  • Deployed our solution with major Enterprises such as Sodexo and GlobalConnect, and leading MSSPs like Orange Cyberdefense

  • Grown to 1,500+ clients across the US and EMEA

  • Ended 2025 with a strong multi-million dollar ARR, and we're targeting $25M by the end of 2027

We're looking for our first Lead, Talent Acquisition (GTM) to build that function from a genuinely blank page: no legacy process to inherit, no five-year-old habits to unlearn, just a fast-growing company and stakeholders who are more than ready to be led.

What you'll actually do

  • Own full-cycle recruiting, hands-on, across every GTM role:AEs, BDRs, RevOps, Enablement and beyond.

  • Partner directly with our Chief People Officerto structure and scale the TA function as we grow, make hiring feel like a system, not a scramble.

  • Build the hiring plan, then run it:forecast the roles, choose the tools, design the process, and get it moving: resourcing, systems and change management all included.

  • Stakeholder education and alignment:you educate and guide stakeholders on recruiting best practices, establishing structured processes and effective hiring standards across the team.

What we're looking for

  • Real GTM or Enterprise recruiting experience:you know hiring a BDR and hiring an Enterprise AE are not the same job, and you've done both well.

  • A track record of structuring or scaling a TA function, inside a high-growth tech company. You've built the playbook, not just run one someone handed you.

  • Sharp project management:you can turn "we need 12 GTM hires by Q1" into a plan with milestones, owners, and a timeline that survives contact with reality.

  • Speed with high standards: you thrive in fast-paced environments with tight deadlines and rapid iteration cycles.

  • Impactful stakeholder management: you seamlessly bring stakeholders into the recruitment process while confidently challenging them when necessary.

  • High data & AI literacy:you use AI in your daily workflow (sourcing, messaging, market mapping), not just as a chatbot, and you know your hiring KPIs.

Why join us

  • A genuine seat at the table: you'll shape how Qevlar hires its entire GTM org, where your hires directly shape revenue.

  • A remote-first, fast-growing scale-up backed by EQT Ventures, Forgepoint Capital and Partech.

  • Leadership that's already bought in: this req exists because the business is willing to invest in doing GTM talent acquisition properly.

  • 70-80K OTE, EMEA-based (France or UK ideally), final number depending on experience. Opportunity for equity and early ownership.

Hiring process

  1. Intro Call

  2. Hiring Manager Interview

  3. Case Study

  4. Culture fit

  5. Reference check and Offer

Translation & Localization Intern, English to French – primarily Systems

(French Language Localization Intern)

Remote | Anywhere in Ontario

Internship: 4–12 Months (Flexible)

Le texte français suit…

At CCIB, we’re dedicated to strengthening and enhancing a prosperous Indigenous economy by fostering business relationships, opportunities, and awareness. As a national Indigenous, non-partisan association, we champion inclusivity and innovation.

Kick-start your career where language, technology, and social impact come together. We’re looking for a Translation & Localization Intern to support the translation and adaptation of organizational systems, platforms, and digital content from English to Canadian French. This role offers an exciting opportunity to contribute to major initiatives, including the roll out of a new CRM system and the development of a new national website.

This opportunity is available to current Ontario University students enrolled in a Translation, Interpretation, Linguistics, French Studies, or related program.What

You’ll Do

  • Translate user-facing content, system labels, forms, workflows, and communications from English to Canadian French
  • Support the French localization of CCIB’s new CRM platform and future digital systems
  • Contribute to the translation and quality review of content for a new organizational website
  • Develop and maintain terminology guides, glossaries, and translation standards
  • Review translations for accuracy, consistency, readability, and cultural relevance
  • Test translated content within systems to ensure functionality, formatting, and user experience are maintained in both official languages.
  • Collaborate with subject matter experts, and project teams to clarify terminology and context
  • Provide recommendations to improve bilingual user experiences across systems and platforms

What You Bring

  • 4th year university student in Translation, Interpretation, Linguistics, French Studies, or a related field
  • Professional-level written French (Canada) and strong English language skills
  • Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to linguistic accuracy
  • Ability to adapt content for diverse audiences while maintaining meaning and intent
  • Strong collaboration and communication skills in a remote environment
  • Interest in technology, digital platforms, user experience, and localization
  • Experience with terminology management, or content management systems is considered an asset

What We Offer

  • Hands-on experience translating enterprise systems and digital platforms
  • The opportunity to contribute to major national projects, including a new CRM and website launch
  • Mentorship and practical experience working with cross-functional teams
  • Meaningful work supporting Indigenous business and economic reconciliation
  • Flexible, remote, and inclusive work environment

Ready to help shape a bilingual digital experience that supports Indigenous business across Canada? Apply today and grow your skills while making a difference.

Indigenous candidates will be given preference

CCIB is committed to an inclusive and accessible recruitment process. If you require accommodations, please let us know in advance. We strongly encourage applications from First Nations, Métis, and Inuit candidates and all other qualified individuals.

Take the next step in your career and join CCIB—where your work will have a lasting impact. Apply today!

Stagiaire en traduction et localisation, de l'anglais vers le français – principalement Systèmes

(Stagiaire en localisation de langue française)

À distance | N'importe où en Ontario

Stage : 4–12 mois (flexible)

Nous nous engageons à renforcer et à améliorer une économie autochtone prospère en favorisant les relations commerciales, les opportunités et la sensibilisation. En tant qu’association nationale autochtone non partisane, nous défendons l’inclusion et l’innovation.

Lancez votre carrière à l'intersection des langues, des technologies et de l'impact social.

Nous sommes à la recherche d'un(e) stagiaire en traduction et localisation pour soutenir la traduction et l'adaptation des systèmes, plateformes et contenus numériques de l'organisation, de l'anglais au français canadien. Ce stage offre une occasion unique de contribuer à des initiatives majeures, notamment le déploiement d'un nouveau système de GRC (Gestion de la relation client) et le développement d'un nouveau site Web national. Ce stage s'adresse aux étudiants universitaires de l'Ontario inscrits dans un programme de traduction, d'interprétation, de linguistique, d'études françaises ou dans un domaine connexe.

Vos responsabilités :

  • Traduire le contenu destiné aux utilisateurs, les étiquettes des systèmes, les formulaires, les flux de travail et les communications de l'anglais vers le français canadien.
  • Soutenir la localisation canadienne de la nouvelle plateforme CRM/GRC et des futurs systèmes numériques.
  • Contribuer à la traduction et à la révision de la qualité du contenu du nouveau site Web de l'organisation.
  • Élaborer et tenir à jour des guides terminologiques, des glossaires et des normes de traduction.
  • Vérifier l'exactitude, la cohérence, la lisibilité et la pertinence culturelle des traductions.
  • Tester les traductions dans les systèmes afin d'assurer le maintien des fonctionnalités, de la mise en forme et de l'expérience utilisateur dans les deux langues officielles.
  • Collaborer avec des experts et des équipes de projet pour clarifier la terminologie et le contexte.
  • Formuler des recommandations pour améliorer l'expérience utilisateur bilingue sur tous les systèmes et plateformes.

Profil recherché :

  • Étudiant(e) de 4e année universitaire en traduction, interprétation, linguistique, études françaises ou domaine connexe.
  • Maîtrise professionnelle du français écrit (Canada) et excellentes compétences en anglais.
  • Sens aigu du détail et engagement envers l'exactitude linguistique.
  • Capacité d'adapter le contenu à divers publics tout en préservant le sens et l'intention.
  • Excellentes compétences en collaboration et en communication, même à distance.
  • Intérêt pour les technologies, les plateformes numériques, l'expérience utilisateur et la localisation.
  • Expérience en gestion terminologique ou en systèmes de gestion de contenu (un atout).

Ce poste vous offre :

  • Expérience pratique de la traduction de systèmes d'entreprise et de plateformes numériques. • Possibilité de contribuer à d'importants projets nationaux, notamment le lancement d'un nouveau système GRC et d'un site Web.
  • Mentorat et expérience pratique au sein d'équipes multidisciplinaires.
  • Travail valorisant au service des entreprises autochtones et de la réconciliation économique.
  • Environnement de travail flexible, à distance et inclusif.

Prêt(e) à contribuer à façonner une expérience bilingue qui soutient les entreprises autochtones partout au Canada ? Postulez dès aujourd'hui et développez vos compétences tout en faisant une différence.

La préférence sera accordée aux candidats autochtones.

Le CCIB/CCEA s'engage à mettre en place un processus de recrutement inclusif et accessible. Si vous avez besoin de mesures d’adaptation, veuillez nous en aviser à l’avance. Nous encourageons fortement les candidatures des membres des Premières Nations, des Métis et des Inuits, ainsi que de toutes les autres personnes qualifiées.

Faites progresser votre carrière et joignez-vous au CCEA, où votre travail aura un impact durable. Postulez dès aujourd'hui!

Salary: $21/hr DOE
